investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available, so pods remained stuck for 141–148 seconds before the eval timed out and returned no evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, and preemption cannot free capacity because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt is immediately Unschedulable, the agent never reaches a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner receives no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState are all missing), causing all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an eval-confirmed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod template is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy the selector, so even if VM capacity were partially available elsewhere, those nodes are excluded. The 4 non-matching nodes cannot be used regardless of their resource state (evidence: failed-check.message).

Tertiary — no preemption victims available: lower-priority pods that could be evicted to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots do not exist on the 2 eligible nodes, so the scheduler cannot self-heal through preemption (evidence: failed-check.message).

Lower confidence — a cluster-level quota or limit range on kata.peerpods.io/vm may have been reduced, shrinking the effective capacity without changing node count. No quota evidence is present in the packet; this would require kubectl inspection to confirm or rule out.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the 2 eligible nodes (kubectl describe nodes) to confirm exhaustion and identify which pods are holding slots.
If slots are confirmed exhausted by live workloads, determine whether any can be safely terminated or scaled down to restore scheduling capacity for new remote-agent pods.

If the node pool is consistently running at full VM capacity, evaluate scaling the peer-pod node pool (adding nodes with the required label and kata.peerpods.io/vm resource) to provide headroom for observability probes and user workloads.
Review the pod's node affinity and node selector configuration to determine whether the restriction to 2 nodes is intentional or whether additional nodes could be labeled to expand the eligible pool.

Investigate whether a cluster-level ResourceQuota or LimitRange is capping kata.peerpods.io/vm below the physical node capacity, which would explain exhaustion even if physical slots appear available.

Once capacity is restored, re-run all three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm the feature returns to a passing state and all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is produced.

Review the eval runner's timeout and retry configuration for remote-agent checks; the current warningLatencyMs=240000 and outageLatencyMs=360000 thresholds (infra/evals/status/features.json line 183) are well above the observed 148 s failure, but adding a faster-failing scheduler-error detection path could reduce probe duration during capacity events.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available (i.e., used < allocatable) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a pod-level resource request mismatch or admission webhook rejection) would need to be investigated.

If the 4 non-matching nodes were found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the pod's node selector were shown to be correct, the failure would be localized to a node labeling or affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run with no other workloads present still produced the same Unschedulable message, it would suggest the node pool itself is misconfigured or the VM resource quota is set to zero rather than being consumed by live workloads.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, the failure would be isolated to the create path rather than a shared scheduling constraint, disproving the shared-capacity-exhaustion diagnosis.
If the eval runner returned a SKIP status (no access token) rather than the scheduler message, the failure would be an eval configuration issue rather than an infrastructure capacity issue.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, so scheduling failures are diagnosed at the resource layer rather than surfaced only as a timed-out pod.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting on node pool shrinkage before it causes full scheduling failure.

Add an eval that monitors the number of currently running remote-agent pods against the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, warning when utilization exceeds a configurable high-water mark (e.g., 80%) to provide advance notice before exhaustion.

Consider a dedicated eval for preemption eligibility: verify that at least one lower-priority pod exists on the eligible nodes so that the scheduler has a preemption path available if capacity is tight.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T17:31–17:36Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to provision a remote agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the Kubernetes swarm cluster, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) calls createAgent with type "remote", which submits a pod that cannot be placed, so the probe times out and returns no evidence, violating the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 264).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: 4 nodes are structurally excluded from scheduling this pod type, leaving only 2 nodes eligible, which amplifies the impact of any capacity pressure on those 2 nodes.

However, the scheduler error message is explicit and specific to pod scheduling, making upstream auth failure unlikely as the primary cause.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available, so pods remained stuck for 141–148 seconds before the eval timed out and returned no evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, and preemption cannot free capacity because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt is immediately Unschedulable, the agent never reaches a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner receives no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState are all missing), causing all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an eval-confirmed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message names the exact resource and node counts.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=156470, status=fail — the check ran for ~156 s and produced no evidence, consistent with a pod stuck unscheduled for 148 s before the probe gave up.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the agent creation API call never completed and the runner never reached the evidence-writing stage.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), latencyMs=146166, no evidence keys — the same capacity constraint blocked a second independent pod.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=148534, no evidence keys — a third independent pod was also blocked, ruling out a transient single-pod anomaly.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: the contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod template is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy the selector, so even if VM capacity were partially available elsewhere, those nodes are excluded. The 4 non-matching nodes cannot be used regardless of their resource state (evidence: failed-check.message).

Tertiary — no preemption victims available: lower-priority pods that could be evicted to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots do not exist on the 2 eligible nodes, so the scheduler cannot self-heal through preemption (evidence: failed-check.message).

Lower confidence — a cluster-level quota or limit range on kata.peerpods.io/vm may have been reduced, shrinking the effective capacity without changing node count. No quota evidence is present in the packet; this would require kubectl inspection to confirm or rule out.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available (i.e., used < allocatable) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a pod-level resource request mismatch or admission webhook rejection) would need to be investigated.

If the 4 non-matching nodes were found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the pod's node selector were shown to be correct, the failure would be localized to a node labeling or affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run with no other workloads present still produced the same Unschedulable message, it would suggest the node pool itself is misconfigured or the VM resource quota is set to zero rather than being consumed by live workloads.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, the failure would be isolated to the create path rather than a shared scheduling constraint, disproving the shared-capacity-exhaustion diagnosis.
If the eval runner returned a SKIP status (no access token) rather than the scheduler message, the failure would be an eval configuration issue rather than an infrastructure capacity issue.

Add an eval that monitors the number of currently running remote-agent pods against the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, warning when utilization exceeds a configurable high-water mark (e.g., 80%) to provide advance notice before exhaustion.

Consider a dedicated eval for preemption eligibility: verify that at least one lower-priority pod exists on the eligible nodes so that the scheduler has a preemption path available if capacity is tight.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the stuck pod showed a different failure reason (e.g., image pull error, OOMKilled, or admission webhook rejection) rather than Unschedulable due to kata.peerpods.io/vm, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened.

If the 2 affinity-matching nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler bug or misconfiguration.
If a concurrent re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest transient contention rather than sustained exhaustion.
If the remote-agent-create sibling check had passed while remote-agent-state failed, it would suggest the failure is in the state-polling logic rather than pod scheduling.

If the eval runner logs showed that requireOrgId threw an error before createAgent was called, the pod scheduling message would be a red herring and the root cause would be an auth or org-resolution failure.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries Kubernetes node capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used, alerting before slots are fully exhausted rather than only when pod scheduling fails.

Add a check that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), catching affinity misconfigurations before they cause scheduling failures.

Add a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes pod scheduling timeout from agent runtime timeout, so future failures can be localized to the scheduling layer vs. the agent initialization layer without manual log inspection.

Consider a canary eval that provisions a minimal remote agent pod on a schedule shorter than the staleAfterMinutes=20 window, providing earlier warning of capacity pressure before the full remote-agent-create/state/runtime chain fails.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T17:31–17:36Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place remote-agent pods on any of the 6 available cluster nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource report insufficient capacity (resource exhaustion), and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity problem that prevents any remote agent VM from being provisioned, causing every downstream eval step—agent creation, state polling, and runtime chat—to time out before producing evidence. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, confirming the failure is not eval-config-specific
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec requires nodes that match a specific label set, but only 2 of 6 nodes qualify, and those 2 are already at capacity. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk. No suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to confirm this hypothesis.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient for the concurrent eval workload, especially if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same VM slots.

Lower probability — eval runner token or org resolution failure causing a silent error before pod creation: ruled out because the scheduler error message is explicit and all three sibling checks share the same scheduling failure, not a token/auth error.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful remote-agent pod scheduling event on the production cluster at the time of the eval run would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.

Cluster node describe output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 capable nodes at 17:31–17:36Z would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis and point instead to a pod spec or affinity misconfiguration.

A passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime immediately after the failure window, without any cluster change, would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.
Evidence that the pod spec's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes would shift the primary cause from resource exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration.
Scheduler logs showing a different rejection reason (e.g., image pull failure, resource quota, or network policy) would disprove the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on each capable node and alerts when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before pod scheduling failures occur.
Add a cluster node readiness eval that verifies the count of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes meets a minimum threshold, catching node label drift or node loss before it impacts agent scheduling.

Add a pod scheduling latency eval that fails fast (e.g., within 30s) if a remote-agent pod does not reach Running state, rather than waiting for the full 141–156s timeout observed in this run, to reduce mean time to detection.

Add a cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods remain in Pending or Terminating state after each eval run, to detect withCleanup failures that could contribute to VM slot exhaustion.
